_comment: One entry per language. `build` runs once in a scratch copy of the language folder; `run` is executed (no shell) with the puzzle input piped to stdin. `kind` groups languages on the site: native = compiled to machine code, vm = bytecode/JIT runtime, interpreted = script interpreter. Set `enabled` to false to drop a language from generation and benchmarking.

languages.name: Python
languages.hint: Read input with sys.stdin.read(). Standard library only (collections, heapq, itertools, functools, re, math are fine). Raise the recursion limit if you recurse deeply.

languages.name: JavaScript
languages.hint: Runs on Node.js. Read input with require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8'). Use BigInt where values can exceed 2^53. No npm packages.

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.hint: Runs directly on Node.js via built-in type stripping, so use only erasable TypeScript syntax: type annotations, interfaces and type aliases are fine; do NOT use enums, namespaces, parameter properties or any other syntax that needs code generation. Import node modules with the 'node:' prefix, e.g. import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'. Use BigInt where values can exceed 2^53. No npm packages.

languages.name: Java
languages.hint: The public class must be named Solution, with no package declaration. Read stdin with a BufferedReader or System.in.readAllBytes(). Use only the JDK.

languages.name: C
languages.hint: Compiled with gcc -O2 using the default GNU C standard. Standard library only, so implement any hash map, heap or dynamic array you need yourself. Read all of stdin into a growing buffer. Use 64-bit integers (long long / int64_t) for answers.

languages.name: C++
languages.hint: Compiled with g++ -O2 -std=c++20. Standard library only (STL containers and algorithms are welcome). Use 64-bit integers for answers.

languages.name: C#
languages.hint: A .NET console project already exists (nullable disabled, implicit usings enabled, top-level statements allowed). Put everything in Program.cs. Read stdin with Console.In.ReadToEnd(). BCL only, no NuGet packages.

languages.name: Go
languages.hint: Single file, package main, standard library only. Read stdin with io.ReadAll(os.Stdin) or a bufio.Scanner with an enlarged buffer.

languages.name: Rust
languages.hint: Compiled directly with rustc, so there is no Cargo and no external crates: std only. Read stdin with std::io::Read::read_to_string.

languages.name: Swift
languages.hint: Single file with top-level code, compiled with swiftc -O on Linux. Foundation is available but keep to the Swift standard library where you can. Read stdin with readLine(strippingNewline: true) in a loop, or FileHandle.standardInput.readDataToEndOfFile().

languages.name: Kotlin
languages.hint: Define a top-level fun main(). Kotlin/JVM, standard library and JDK only. Read stdin with System.`in`.bufferedReader().readText().

languages.name: Ruby
languages.hint: Read input with $stdin.read. Standard library only (set, etc. via require).

languages.name: PHP
languages.hint: CLI script starting with <?php. Read input with stream_get_contents(STDIN). Print with echo and PHP_EOL.

languages.name: Bash
languages.hint: Bash 5 only. Use builtins, arrays, associative arrays and arithmetic expansion. Small coreutils helpers (sort, tr, cut, grep, sed, wc, head, tail) are allowed when they clearly help, but do NOT call awk, perl, python or any other interpreter. Read input with mapfile -t lines or read -r.

languages.name: Haskell
languages.hint: module Main with main :: IO (). Only packages that ship with GHC (base, containers, array, bytestring, text, mtl) are available. Read stdin with getContents or Data.ByteString.Char8.getContents. Use strict folds and Data.Map.Strict/IntMap to keep it fast.

languages.name: Scala
languages.hint: Scala 3. Define `object Solution { def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = ... }` (do not use @main). Standard library only. Read stdin with scala.io.Source.stdin.mkString.

languages.name: R
languages.hint: Base R only, no packages. Read stdin with readLines(file('stdin')). Print answers with cat(x, '\n', sep='') and format large numbers with format(x, scientific = FALSE) or sprintf('%.0f', x) so they never come out in exponent notation.

languages.name: Lua
languages.hint: Lua 5.4 (64-bit integers, integer division //). Read input with io.read('a'). Standard library only.

languages.name: Dart
languages.hint: Define void main() and import 'dart:io'. Read stdin by looping stdin.readLineSync() until null. Core libraries only, no pub packages.

languages.name: Perl
languages.hint: Perl 5 with `use strict; use warnings;`. Core modules only (List::Util, etc.). Read stdin with local $/; <STDIN>.

languages.name: Elixir
languages.hint: An .exs script run with `elixir`. Read stdin with IO.read(:stdio, :eof). Standard library only, no Mix dependencies. Prefer Enum/Stream pipelines, MapSet and Map, and tail-recursive loops.

languages.name: OCaml
languages.hint: Native-compiled. Stdlib plus the str and unix libraries only. Read stdin with In_channel.input_all stdin (OCaml 4.14+) or a loop over input_line.

languages.name: Julia
languages.hint: Base and standard-library modules only, no Pkg. Wrap the work in functions (type-stable, no mutable globals in hot loops). Read stdin with read(stdin, String).

languages.name: Zig
languages.hint: std only. The Zig standard library changes a lot between releases, so write against the exact version in the toolchain line above. Use std.heap.page_allocator or an arena over it, read all of stdin into memory, and print the two answers to stdout.

languages.name: Fortran
languages.hint: Free-form Fortran 2008 compiled with gfortran, `program main` with implicit none. Read stdin lines with read(*,'(A)',iostat=ios) into a long character buffer. Use integer(kind=8) for answers.
